about.title: Palos Verdes Estates Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Palos Verdes Estates is a small community in Los Angeles County, and the public record reflects that: in 2025 the city logged 11 injury collisions with 12 people hurt and no traffic deaths. Yet a wrongful death claim rarely depends on how a city's roads compare. Families here lose someone to a crash on Palos Verdes Drive West that happened on the way home, to a fall at a property that was never repaired, to a medical error, or to a defective product. When negligence takes a life, California law gives a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children the first right to bring a civil claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when there is no spouse or child. The clock is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Palos Verdes Estates families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so you can grieve while someone else manages the paperwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Palos Verdes Estates Use LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out standing before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter when a government entity may share fault. An attorney can calendar those dates from your very first conversation.

items.title: A full picture of the loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support your loved one would have provided and the love, companionship, and guidance your family lost. Contingency representation means no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Palos Verdes Estates recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can my family still have a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Yes. Wrongful death claims arise from many situations besides crashes, including medical negligence, unsafe property, defective products, and care facility neglect. A death that occurred outside the city, or on a road like Palos Verdes Drive West or Granvia Altamira in a later year, is also evaluated on its own facts. What matters is whether someone's carelessness caused the loss.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs separately from any criminal prosecution, and it does not depend on a conviction. The two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court, so it is wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if a city or county agency may have played a role in the death?
items.answer: Claims involving a government entity in California follow a different, much shorter process that begins with an administrative claim, often within six months. Missing that step can close the door on the case entirely. An attorney can quickly determine whether any public agency is involved and act within the required time.
